blocks.text: TAEP Farmers Market Promotion & Retail Grant Program — Fiscal Year 2014-2015 1. Describe your organization. The Nashville Farmers’ Market (NFM) is operated by the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County and opened at its current location in 1995. The Farmers’ Market facility covers over sixteen acres of urban land and is composed of a 38,000 square foot interior, enclosed Market House,” flanked by four covered exterior retail sheds (each measuring about 15,000 square feet). In 2015, construction will begin to fully enclose and condition the Southeast retail sheds with a projected completion date of June, 2015. The Market House is climate-controlled and exterior sheds are open-air. All flooring is concrete. NEM is fully handicap-accessible and has only one permanent sign (a Rosa L. Parks Blvd. electronic marquee). There are currently over three hundred free parking spaces on the property with access to additional forty spaces on 7" Avenue. NFM currently has nine restrooms which will increase to eleven post-shed enclosure. NFM is currently open seven days/week, 362 days/year. The Farmers’ Market management team consists of a five full-time employees. NFM receives oversight and governance support from a Nashville Farmers’ Market Board whose members are appointed by the Mayor and include; a Davidson County farmer & rancher, two Davidson County restaurantowners, and other community members. blocks.text: TAEP Farmers Market Promotion & Retail Grant Program Fiscal Year 2014-2015 3. Describe your proposed project(s), List each proposed project individually. Indicate how the project(s) will benefit your market’s vendors and help increase their farm income. 1. Advertising & Promotion-Electronic Mediums: Expand market targeting and segmentation, increase consumer education and engagement through electronic mediums: According to 2013 survey results, the majority of NFM customers live within a ten-mile radius; and work within a four-mile radius of NFM. With the explosive residential growth of adjacent Germantown, downtown and west areas; newly constructed local amenities like the upcoming baseball field; expanded transit plans and routes around NFM; we expect an increase in the need for; and our abilities to offer more seasonal programming and events throughout peak season utilizing extended hours and a thematic marketing focus. Producers themselves tell us sales are immediately impacted in a positive way when they are included and promoted using this strategic outlet; and results of profiles, features, and “talking store” cumulatively Positive in long-term was as well. Thus, a solid, cost-effective and comprehensive marketing and promotional electronic medium is required to support these efforts; and we request to do so using grant funds in 2015.

1. Describe your organization. The Nashville Farmers’ Market (NFM) is operated by the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County and opened at its current location in 1995. The Farmers’ Market facility covers over sixteen acres of urban land and is composed of a 38,000 square foot interior, enclosed Market House,” flanked by four covered exterior retail sheds (each measuring about 15,000 square feet). In 2015, construction will begin to fully enclose and condition the Southeast retail sheds with a projected completion date of June, 2015. The Market House is climate-controlled and exterior sheds are open-air. All flooring is concrete. NEM is fully handicap-accessible and has only one permanent sign (a Rosa L. Parks Blvd. electronic marquee). There are currently over three hundred free parking spaces on the property with access to additional forty spaces on 7" Avenue. NFM currently has nine restrooms which will increase to eleven post-shed enclosure. NFM is currently open seven days/week, 362 days/year. The Farmers’ Market management team consists of a five full-time employees. NFM receives oversight and governance support from a Nashville Farmers’ Market Board whose members are appointed by the Mayor and include; a Davidson County farmer & rancher, two Davidson County restaurant- owners, and other community members. In 2015, an advisory committee of merchants will begin that will assist in planning and supporting “green market” initiatives—making NFM a more environmentally-conscious operation and community education center. A portion of this education will include benefits related to buying locally-sourced farm products and foods. The overriding organizational goal of 2015 is to continue NFM’s efforts towards becoming the Southeast’s premier farmers’ market and Tennessee’s central source and retail outlet for farmers, artisans, and crafters throughout all seasons. In 2015—NFM plans to become ever more a producer-only market by allocating increased shed spaces for local farm products, plant material, locally-made foods and crafts. In 2014-2015 NFM will increase the number of locally-owned and operated restaurants and shops inside our Market House from fifteen to twenty. All Market House merchants are encouraged to source from NFM farmers and artisans and the proportion of these merchants doing so has tripled in the last two years. For new and upcoming merchants, sourcing from NFM has become a formal part of criteria for eligibility. In 2012, Grow Local Kitchen at NFM opened offering a rental kitchen available for production, culinary education classes, events, “pop-up” restaurants, and catering made with farm-fresh and local ingredients. Over the last two years, the number of producers using Grow Local Kitchen has tripled. Our popular Night Market series always features a farmer and farm- products in Grow Local Kitchen; customers have come to expect and celebrate this special guest monthly. Some farmers are small production farmers visit Market one or two days/week. Specialty- crop farmers may retail their product seven days a week while their product is in season.
